stemMd: At a chemical synapse, what usually triggers release of neurotransmitter from the presynaptic terminal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Removal of every vesicle from the terminal

options.label: B
options.textMd: Direct conversion of sodium ions into neurotransmitter molecules

options.label: D
options.textMd: Entry of calcium ions following arrival of an action potential

options.label: E
options.textMd: Fusion of the two neurons into one cell

explanationMd: Depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels in the presynaptic terminal. Calcium entry promotes fusion of transmitter-containing vesicles with the membrane. Released transmitter then diffuses across the cleft and binds receptors on the postsynaptic cell.

distractorRationale.e: Typical chemical synapses preserve separate cells.
distractorRationale.c: Chromosome replication is not the rapid synaptic trigger.
distractorRationale.a: Vesicles are needed for neurotransmitter release.
distractorRationale.b: Ions are not converted into organic neurotransmitters by the action potential.
